title: Sunny Desert Friends!
intro: Hi, friends! I'm Milo the bluebird, and welcome to The Animated Zoo!
Today we're visiting animals that live in hot, sunny, dry places!
Can you count five animals with me? One, two, three, four, five!

lines: Here's our first animal. Here's a clue: it has a big hump on its back! Can you guess?
Let's walk over to the camels!
Camels can go a long, long time without food or water.
Camels can walk for miles every day, and they can run as fast as a horse!
Can you walk tall and slow like a camel? Step, step!
Can you guess how many humps this camel has?
One hump! A camel with one hump is called a dromedary.
Bactrian camels are different. They have two humps!
And camels have a bony bump over each eye, like a built-in sun hat.
Who's next? Here's a clue: it's small, it stands up tall, and it loves to dig! Can you guess?
Let's scurry over to the meerkats!
Meerkats live together in big family groups.
They dig lots of little tunnels in the ground, so they always have a place to hide.
Can you stand up tall like a meerkat? Up on your tiptoes!
Can you guess what one meerkat does while the others look for food?
It stands guard! One meerkat climbs up high and watches out for the family.
The lookout makes a soft little call every few seconds. That means everything is okay!
Meerkats take turns being the lookout. Good teamwork!
Who's next? Here's a clue: it's a bird with long legs and a long neck, but it can't fly! Can you guess?
Let's run over to the ostriches!
Ostriches take really big steps. One step can be more than ten feet long. That is longer than a big bed!
Can you take one giant step like an ostrich? Big step!
Ostriches have just two toes on each foot.
Can you guess? Do ostriches really hide their heads in the sand?
No! That's just a silly story. Ostriches put their heads down to check on their eggs in the nest.
Ostrich moms and dads take turns keeping the eggs warm.
Who's next? Here's a clue: it hops, hops, hops! Can you guess?
Let's hop over to the kangaroos!
Red kangaroos live in hot, dry parts of Australia.
A baby kangaroo is called a joey. It grows up in its mom's pouch.
Can you hop like a kangaroo? Hop, hop, hop!
Can you guess what a red kangaroo does to cool off on a hot day?
It licks its arms! When the wet fur dries, it helps the kangaroo cool down.
You cool down a little bit like that too, when you sweat.
Kangaroos are smart about staying cool!
Our last animal has a big fluffy mane! Can you guess?
Let's tiptoe over to the lions!
A boy lion's mane gets thicker and darker as he grows older.
Some lions that live in very hot, dry places have hardly any mane at all.
Can you shake your head like a lion with a big mane? Shake, shake!
Can you guess what's special about a lion's tail?
It has a fluffy tuft at the tip! Lions are the only cats with a tail tuft.
Lions are also the only cats that live together in big family groups.
Scientists think lions may wave their tail tufts to send signals to each other.

recap: What a sunny adventure! Let's remember.
Some camels have one hump, and some have two.
Meerkats take turns being the lookout.
Ostriches don't hide their heads in the sand.
Red kangaroos lick their arms to cool off.
And lions have a fluffy tuft on their tails!
outro: Which desert animal was your favorite? Remember, be kind to every animal. Watch quietly and give them space.
Bye, friends! See you at the zoo!
